Have an agent open Lichess and start a game
A user told Operator to go to Lichess and play a game; it opened the site, started a blitz game and made the first move.
Done with
OP
Operator
What they did
The Reddit post is a firsthand report comparing an older, heavily scripted Operator prompt with a newer run where the user simply typed, go to Lichess and play a game. The poster says the agent then opened Lichess, started a blitz game, and made the first move on its own, with no special formatting or step-by-step prompt; the comments shown do not add procedural detail.
How it went
The reported outcome was that it completed the setup and first move of a blitz game from a plain-language instruction. The post gives no timing, score, or evidence beyond the author’s description and screenshots.
Worth knowing
The main catch is that the source provides only a brief anecdotal description, so if you want to copy it, you are relying on a simple prompt plus whatever browser control the Operator already had.
Try it yourself
with
Operator
Copy prompt
Go to [a game site, e.g. lichess.org], start a [game type, e.g. 10-minute blitz] game against [a random opponent or the computer], and make the opening move. Stop after the first move and tell me what you played and what the board looks like. Do not create an account, enter payment details, or accept any prompts to sign up without showing me first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ArtificialInteligence/comments/1ku1oz2
